_comment: Navigation sweep profile for Excitebike (ADR-0239, PRD Part A slice
F14.16). Read by scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py.
RUNG 1, NOT RUNG 2. ADR-0239 s1 says to use the first rung that reaches
the place, and for Excitebike that is rung 1: the game's own selector, by
input. navigation.kind is 'input', so no cheat rides with any session and
every session is an ADR-0184 s2 'clean' pass that all four surfaces may
read. Rung 2 is not available: no published RAM map names the current
track. Both Excitebike RAM maps that exist were read on 2026-09-26 -
Data Crystal, 'Excitebike (NES)/RAM map'
(https://datacrystal.tcrf.net/wiki/Excitebike_(NES)/RAM_map, via the
Wayback Machine: the live page is behind a JS challenge) and the ROM
Detectives Wiki, 'Excitebike (NES) - RAM'
(http://www.romdetectives.com/Wiki/index.php?title=Excitebike_(NES)_-_RAM)
- and neither has a track index. Data Crystal's $00B0 'lane, which track
you are in, 1-4' is the lane inside a track, not the track; the ROM
Detectives map lists $0070 'Lane (0-4)' for the same thing and no track
byte at all. So rung 2 would need an invented address, which ADR-0184 s5
refuses.
THE SELECTOR THE GAME OFFERS. Read off this ROM's own screens (screenshots
kept under runs/f1416/excitebike/probe, 2026-09-26) and the Excitebike
instruction booklet (Nintendo of America, 1985; archive.org, item
'compilation-of-game-manuals-for-mini-consoles-english-only', file
'Excitebike CLV-P-NAAHE_text.pdf'):
title menu     'SELECTION A / SELECTION B / DESIGN'. The booklet: 'Move
the checkered flag to line up with the game you wish to
play ... SELECTION A is a solo run game. SELECTION B has
competing motocross riders. DESIGN mode is for
programming your own course.'
track select   '*** CHALLENGE RACE ***' over 'TRACK#' and 1 2 3 4 5.
The booklet calls this the preliminary race: 'Before
entering the Excitebike race, you must first qualify in
the preliminary challenge race ... Choose the challenge
race from 1 to 5 that you wish to start with.' The same
screen serves SELECTION A and SELECTION B (identical
screenshot checksum 0x7042C330 at frame 300), which is
why one entry script per track covers both.
DESIGN menu    'PLAY MODE A / PLAY MODE B / DESIGN / SAVE / LOAD /
RESET'. The booklet: 'The DESIGN mode menu will appear.
Move the checkered flag to DESIGN again and press the
START button' ... 'Save and Load menu selections are not
operable in this game'.
editor         'Figure selection screen'. The booklet: 19 hurdles
lettered A-S, A moves the rider, B sets the hurdle, and
LP sets the lap count up to 9.
The eleven stamp scripts here walk that tree from power-on. Every press
is 20 frames with a 40-frame gap: the ROM ignores a Start that arrives
inside the frame a menu cursor move is being read (measured 2026-09-26 -
Down at frame 60-69 then Start at 70-79 left the title menu where it
was, while the same pair 40 frames apart moved it).
THE STAGES THIS REACHES, and what is NOT here. Thirteen values: the five
CHALLENGE RACE tracks under SELECTION A, the same five under SELECTION B
(verified to be the same five: the two sessions' screenshots share a
palette and B adds the CPU riders' colours), the editor, and the two
design PLAY MODEs. NOT recorded, with the reason: the five MAIN races.
The booklet reaches them only by placing third or better in the
preliminary ('If you place third or better in the preliminary, you go to
the main race of the same number'), which is a stage-clear transition a
blind body does not produce - ADR-0239 s1 rung 3 work that a later
measurement has to name, exactly like the stage-clear transition itself.
THE RAM CHECKS, AND WHAT THEY DO NOT PROVE. No published byte names the
track, so no ramCheck here identifies one. Each proves the mode the
session ended in, and the track identity rests on the stamp script, the
per-track palette the recordings draw in, and ADR-0239 s4's 'new' count:
track-a*/track-b*   $004F = 01. ROM Detectives: '004F - Racing Flag
(00 - At Starting Line, 01 - Racing)'. A session
that never left the title menu or the track select
reads 00.
design,             $0057 = 01. ROM Detectives: '0057 - Laps remaining
design-play-*       in design mode'. The editor draws the same number
as its own 'LP 1', one lap being what a design
opens with; a CHALLENGE RACE three-lap session
reads 02, so the value separates the design screen
set from the ten track sessions.
(both)              the race clock is published as $0068 minutes,
$0069 seconds, $006A hundredths, and was read off
the probes: the ten track sessions end at 0:11:42
or 0:12:30, the editor at 0:00:00. A ramCheck is
one address, so the clock is evidence in the
measurement log rather than a check here.
Both addresses are CONSEQUENCE bytes - the game writes them because the
session left the menu, not because anything pinned them. That matters: a
RAM pin substitutes the byte on the CPU's read bus and never writes memory,
so a check on the pinned address reads either the game's own value or a byte
the game stored back after reading the pin, and that one state cannot tell
the two apart (measured on Contra: `cheat=0030:05` plays stage 6 while the
final state's $0030 still reads 00, where Punch-Out's fight loader stores
the byte back - issue #546). This profile has no pins at all, so neither
reading can arise here; it is written down because a later profile that adds
a pin must read its check knowing which of the two it is looking at, and the
sweep's caveat now names the pinned byte so it can.
A FAILING CHECK IS NOT ALWAYS A BROKEN RUN. $004F returns to 00 when a
race ends, so a 120 s body that finishes its three laps and lands on a
result screen reports 00; ADR-0239 s4's 'new' count is the behavioural
test that keeps that case from being read as a warp that failed.
NO LIVES PIN, so ADR-0239 s3's inert control does not apply. Excitebike
has no lives counter: a session is one race, it ends when the laps are
done or the clock runs out, and there is no GAME OVER screen for a pin
to foreclose. defaults.cheats is therefore absent, and no process in
this sweep is launched with a cheat at all.
CAVEAT THAT APPLIES TO EVERY SESSION. A stage that is entered rather
than played never shows the stage-clear transition, and these sessions
enter: the run starts at the picked stage and the body never finishes
three laps to a result screen on purpose, so the result and main-race
screens are the one part of the game this sweep leaves to the game's
own stage-1 route and to a later rung-3 measurement.

navigation.label: title menu (SELECTION A / SELECTION B / DESIGN) and the CHALLENGE RACE track select (TRACK 1-5)
navigation.source: Excitebike instruction booklet (Nintendo of America, 1985), '3. HOW TO PLAY' and '4. DESIGN MODE' - the checkered flag picks SELECTION A, SELECTION B or DESIGN and START begins, the preliminary challenge race is chosen from 1 to 5, and the DESIGN mode menu's own DESIGN entry opens the figure selection screen. Corroborated by this ROM's own screens, read 2026-09-26: 'SELECTION A / SELECTION B / DESIGN' at the title, '*** CHALLENGE RACE ***' with 'TRACK# 1 2 3 4 5' on the track select, and 'PLAY MODE A / PLAY MODE B / DESIGN / SAVE / LOAD / RESET' on the DESIGN mode menu. ADR-0239 s1 rung 1: input, no cheat.
